historical_evidence.company: Founded 2010 by Patrick and John Collison, providing developer-first APIs for accepting and processing online payments, by this point an established and widely-adopted platform among internet businesses.
historical_evidence.market: Large, growing global digital-payments market, with entrenched incumbents (PayPal, traditional merchant processors) but continued strong secular growth in e-commerce and internet-native businesses as the underlying demand driver.
historical_evidence.team: Founders had by this point run the company for six years, through multiple funding rounds and demonstrated an ability to scale both the product and the organization.
historical_evidence.product: Mature, widely-adopted developer-first payments API platform with a strong reputation for documentation and integration speed, differentiated primarily on developer experience relative to legacy payment processors.
historical_evidence.execution: Raised $150M in a Series D round in November 2016, co-led by CapitalG (Alphabet's late-stage investment arm) and existing investor General Catalyst, at a $9.2 billion post-money valuation — up from a $5 billion valuation the prior year, alongside a separate revolving credit facility of up to $250M from J.P. Morgan, Goldman Sachs, Morgan Stanley, and Barclays.
historical_evidence.traction: No specific payment-volume or merchant-count figures were found in the contemporaneous sources reviewed for the November 2016 snapshot specifically.
historical_evidence.financial: The near-doubling of valuation year-over-year (from $5B to $9.2B) alongside a large institutional credit facility from four major banks is a strong, real-time-visible signal of sustained investor and lender confidence in the company's scale and financial trajectory.
